response.consequence: In the rule list, users cannot pause or export Grafana recording rules from the actions menu, although they could before. Silence being alerting-only is correct. Pause, export and permanent delete should not be limited to alerting rules.
response.explanation: In useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` gates ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently (lines 324-330). The ruler hook it was adapted from used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which matches every Grafana-managed rule, recording rules included. For a Grafana recording rule, `isAlertingRule` is false, so those abilities report as not supported. The new GrafanaRuleListItem passes recording rules to RuleActionsButtons and AlertRuleMenu with only promRule. The list view no longer calls the ruler API, so there is no ruler ability to fall back on. This is a permission-evaluation regression, not an authorization bypass: the new code is stricter than before, not looser.
response.title: Pause, Export and Restore abilities for Grafana prom rules are limited to alerting rules, so recording rules lose them

response.consequence: Update, Delete, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently report as supported for rules in federated rule groups. The UI shows edit and delete actions that were previously hidden, and the backend can reject them. This is a regression in the capability check.
response.explanation: The old useAllAlertRuleAbilities computed isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) from the CombinedRule. The change turns it into a wrapper around useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false (with a TODO). useAllAlertRuleAbilities and its callers (useAlertRuleAbility and useAlertRuleAbilities, lines 180 and 188) still receive a CombinedRule with a group, but the group is no longer consulted. A rule in a federated Mimir rule group therefore no longer counts as immutable.
response.title: Federated rule group check dropped from useAllAlertRuleAbilities

response.explanation: The updated mocks match the hooks that RuleActionsButtons and AlertRuleMenu use. The Grafana and cloud tests each set the matching plural and singular hooks. I found no test that cannot fail.

Clicking it calls setShowSilenceDrawer(true). The drawer only renders when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true, and `rule` is undefined in the promRule-only case. So nothing opens.
